certifications.name: GDPR Compliance

flags: Bill.com is not fully HIPAA compliant. The platform offers safeguards for ePHI and requires a BAA for healthcare organizations, but certification is absent and the company is still 'working towards' compliance.

Third-party vendor profiles (e.g., Nudge Security) claim Bill.com holds ISO 27001 certification, but this is not confirmed on bill.com's own domain. The DPA mentions ISO 27001 as an industry standard for service providers to follow, not as Bill.com's own certification.
Third-party sources claim FedRAMP and CSA STAR certifications, but the bill.com domain has no public evidence for either.
Data residency is not explicitly stated; the platform is only described as 'cloud-based.'

Bill.com has a strong GDPR compliance posture (DPA, SCCs, EU representatives) but is not formally 'GDPR certified'; it complies with the regulation's legal requirements rather than holding a certification.
The privacy policy is silent on customer data use for AI training, notable given Bill.com's marketing of AI-powered features.
